questions.q: What is a Glue database, in the context of this lesson?
options: Another name for the S3 bucket itself
A Redshift cluster used to hold the crawler's output
A logical namespace in the Glue Data Catalog where table definitions are registered — not a running database engine
A running relational database engine that stores copies of the CSV rows
questions.explain: northfield_raw_db is just a namespace for organizing table metadata in the Catalog — it holds no data of its own.

questions.q: What permissions does the crawler's IAM role actually need?
options: Read access to the specific S3 raw-zone path, plus permission to read/write the Glue Catalog — nothing more
Full administrator access to the entire AWS account
Write access to Redshift and Step Functions
Permission to delete objects from any S3 bucket in the account
questions.explain: Least privilege means scoping the role to exactly what the crawler does: read the raw files, write Catalog metadata.

questions.q: What name does Glue give the table created by the crawler against s3://northfield-raw-zone/orders-raw/, and why?
options: northfield_raw_db — the table is always named after its database
orders_2026-08-01 — named after the first file alphabetically
orders_raw — Glue names the table after the S3 prefix folder by default
The table has no name until a human assigns one manually
questions.explain: Glue's default naming convention uses the S3 prefix folder name, which is why the table ends up called orders_raw.

questions.q: Why does this crawler run on demand rather than on a schedule?
options: The raw files are a one-time August export that isn't changing daily, so a recurring schedule would cost a little for no benefit
Scheduled crawlers are more expensive than Athena queries regardless of use case
Glue Crawlers are not capable of running on a schedule at all
On-demand crawlers can only target a single file, never a whole prefix
questions.explain: Scheduling makes sense once ingestion is recurring; for a static one-time export, a manual on-demand run is the right fit.

questions.q: What four stages does the crawler move through when it runs?
options: Queued, Transforming, Loading, Published
Pending, Encrypting, Partitioning, Complete
Starting, Running, Stopping, Ready
Draft, Review, Approved, Archived
questions.explain: Those four stages are visible in the Glue console while the crawler samples files and infers the schema.
